title: Dispatch BBA 7: Market Evacuated as Hospital Doors Appear
summary: The planned correction failed when a second register opened on the square.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The attempt to close the ward was interrupted at dawn yesterday. Before Miss Morrow could enter Elsie Gray's name, a second door appeared on the north side of the square. Through it, the Institute saw a second ward identical to the first, with its own slate, its own beds, and its own intake register.

Inspector Voss cleared the market while Dr. Saye measured the opening. The ward's intake slate now bore sixty-three names, all belonging to living residents of Alderwick. The bell began sounding continuously, not in strokes but in a low hum that traveled through the paving stones.

Sister Kells came to the doorway carrying the discharge ledger. She could not cross into the square. "The ward has found more patients," she said. "It has been calling anyone who walked over its ground. The register will not close until every name is accounted for."

Mrs. Arden supplied Elsie's baptism certificate and a letter in which Elsie described the night of the fire. Sister Kells read the letter through the doorway. "She remembers me," Sister Kells said. "That is enough. The ward needs only one true record to release the rest."

The council has kept the square closed. Sister Kells has agreed to write from within. Miss Morrow will return this morning with the discharge date prepared. The Institute has asked residents to avoid the square until the bell is silent.
